verses.zh: 弟兄们，我把　神赐给马其顿众教会的恩告诉你们，
verses.en: Now we make known to you, brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] the grace of God given to the churches of Macedonia,
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:8.

verses.zh: 就是他们在患难中受大试炼的时候，仍有满足的快乐，在极穷之间还格外显出他们乐捐的厚恩。
verses.en: that during a severe ordeal of suffering, their abundant joy and their extreme poverty have overflowed in the wealth[NOTE:1] of their generosity.
notes: Or “riches.”

verses.zh: 我可以证明，他们是按着力量，而且也过了力量，自己甘心乐意地捐助，
verses.en: For I testify, they gave according to their means and beyond their means. They did so voluntarily,[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “spontaneously.”

verses.zh: 再三地求我们，准他们在这供给圣徒的恩情上有分；
verses.en: begging us with great earnestness for the blessing and fellowship of helping[NOTE:1] the saints.
notes: Or “of ministering to.”

verses.zh: 并且他们所做的，不但照我们所想望的，更照　神的旨意先把自己献给主，又归附了我们。
verses.en: And they did this not just as we had hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and to us by the will of God.

verses.zh: 因此我劝提多，既然在你们中间开办这慈惠的事，就当办成了。
verses.en: Thus[NOTE:1] we urged[NOTE:2] Titus that, just as he had previously begun this work,[NOTE:3] so also he should complete this act of kindness[NOTE:4] for you.
notes: A new sentence was started here in the translation and the word “thus” was supplied to indicate that it expresses the result of the previous clause.
Or “we exhorted.”
The words “this work” are not in the Greek text but are implied. Direct objects in Greek were often omitted and must be supplied from the context.
Grk “this grace.”

verses.zh: 你们既然在信心、口才、知识、热心，和待我们的爱心上，都格外显出满足来，就当在这慈惠的事上也格外显出满足来。
verses.en: But as you excel[NOTE:1] in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, and in all eagerness and in the love from us that is in you[NOTE:2]—make sure that you excel[NOTE:3] in this act of kindness[NOTE:4] too.
notes: Grk “as you abound.”

The reading “the love from us that is in you” is very difficult in this context, for Paul is here enumerating the Corinthians’ attributes: How is it possible for them to excel “in the love from us that is in you”? Most likely, because of this difficulty, several early scribes, as well as most later ones (א C D F G Ψ [33] M lat), altered the text to read “your love for us” (so NIV84; Grk ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐν ἡμῖν ἀγάπῃ [ex humōn en hēmin agapē]). The reading ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν ἀγάπῃ (ex hēmōn en humin agapē) is found, however, in excellent and early witnesses (P46 B 0243 6 104 630 1175 1739 1881 co). As the harder reading it explains the rise of the other reading. What, then, is the force of “in the love from us that is in you”? Most likely, Paul is commending the Corinthians for excelling in deriving some inspiration from the apostles’ love for them. NIV11 renders the phrase “the love we have kindled in you.”
Grk “you abound.”
Grk “this grace.”

verses.zh: 我说这话，不是吩咐你们，乃是藉着别人的热心试验你们爱心的实在。
verses.en: I am not saying this as a command, but I am testing the genuineness of your love by comparison with the eagerness of others.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “by means of the eagerness of others.”

verses.zh: 你们知道我们主耶稣基督的恩典：他本来富足，却为你们成了贫穷，叫你们因他的贫穷，可以成为富足。
verses.en: For you know the grace[NOTE:1] of our Lord Jesus Christ, that although he was rich, he became poor for your sakes, so that you by his poverty could become rich.
notes: Or “generosity.”

verses.zh: 我在这事上把我的意见告诉你们，是与你们有益；因为你们下手办这事，而且起此心意，已经有一年了，
verses.en: So here is my opinion on this matter: It is to your advantage, since you[NOTE:1] made a good start last year both in your giving and your desire to give,
notes: Grk “who.”

verses.zh: 如今就当办成这事。既有愿做的心，也当照你们所有的去办成。
verses.en: to finish what you started,[NOTE:1] so that just as you wanted to do it eagerly,[NOTE:2] you can also complete it according to your means.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “and now also complete the doing.”
Grk “just as the eagerness to want [it].”
Grk “complete from what you have.”

verses.zh: 因为人若有愿做的心，必蒙悦纳，乃是照他所有的，并不是照他所无的。
verses.en: For if the eagerness is present, the gift itself[NOTE:1] is acceptable according to whatever one has, not according to what he does not have.
notes: The words “the gift itself” are not in the Greek text but are implied. Translators often supply an English phrase like “it is” (NASB) but in the context, Paul is clearly referring to the collection Titus was to oversee (2 Cor 8:4-7). Therefore there is no reason not to specify the referent (the gift) more narrowly for clarity.

verses.zh: 我原不是要别人轻省，你们受累，
verses.en: For I do not say this so there would be relief for others and suffering for you, but as a matter of equality.

verses.zh: 乃要均平，就是要你们的富余，现在可以补他们的不足，使他们的富余，将来也可以补你们的不足，这就均平了。
verses.en: At the present time, your abundance will meet their need,[NOTE:1] so that one day their abundance may also meet your need, and thus there may be equality,
notes: Or “their lack.”

verses.zh: 如经上所记：多收的也没有余；少收的也没有缺。
verses.en: as it is written: “The one who gathered[NOTE:1] much did not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have too little.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The word “gathered” is not in the Greek text, but is implied (so also for the second occurrence of the word later in the verse).
A quotation from Exod 16:18.

verses.zh: 多谢　神，感动提多的心，叫他待你们殷勤，像我一样。
verses.en: But thanks be to God who put in the heart of Titus the same devotion[NOTE:1] I have for you,
notes: Or “eagerness.”

verses.zh: 他固然是听了我的劝，但自己更是热心，情愿往你们那里去。
verses.en: because he not only accepted our request, but since he was very eager,[NOTE:1] he is coming[NOTE:2] to you of his own accord.[NOTE:3]
notes: The comparative form of this adjective is used here with elative meaning.
This verb has been translated as an epistolary aorist.
Or “of his own free will.”

verses.zh: 我们还打发一位兄弟和他同去，这人在福音上得了众教会的称赞。
verses.en: And we are sending[NOTE:1] along with him the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in spreading the gospel.[NOTE:2]
notes: This verb has been translated as an epistolary aorist.
Grk “the brother of whom the praise in the gospel [is] throughout all the churches.”

verses.zh: 不但这样，他也被众教会挑选，和我们同行，把所托与我们的这捐赀送到了，可以荣耀主，又表明我们乐意的心。
verses.en: In addition,[NOTE:1] this brother[NOTE:2] has also been chosen by the churches as our traveling companion as we administer this generous gift[NOTE:3] to the glory of the Lord himself and to show our readiness to help.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “gospel, and not only this, but.” Here a new sentence was started in the translation.
Grk “he”; the referent (the brother mentioned in v. 18) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
That is, the offering or collection being taken to assist impoverished Christians.
The words “to help” are not in the Greek text but are implied (see L&N 25.68).

verses.zh: 这就免得有人因我们收的捐银很多，就挑我们的不是。
verses.en: We did this[NOTE:1] as a precaution so that no one should blame us in regard to this generous gift we are administering.
notes: “This” refers to sending the brother mentioned in 2 Cor 8:18 to Corinth along with Titus. The words “We did this” have no equivalent in the Greek text, but are necessary to maintain the thought flow in English. The Greek participle that begins v. 20 continues the sentence begun in v. 18 which concerns the sending of the other brother mentioned there.

verses.zh: 我们留心行光明的事，不但在主面前，就在人面前也是这样。
verses.en: For we are concerned about what is right not only before the Lord but also before men.[NOTE:1]
notes: An allusion to Prov 3:4.

gr.gloss: We are taking great care to do

verses.zh: 我们又打发一位兄弟同去；这人的热心，我们在许多事上屡次试验过。现在他因为深信你们，就更加热心了。
verses.en: And we are sending[NOTE:1] with them our brother whom we have tested many times and found eager in many matters, but who now is much more eager than ever because of the great confidence he has in you.
notes: This verb has been translated as an epistolary aorist.

verses.zh: 论到提多，他是我的同伴，一同为你们劳碌的。论到那两位兄弟，他们是众教会的使者，是基督的荣耀。
verses.en: If there is any question[NOTE:1] about Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you; if there is any question about our brothers, they are messengers[NOTE:2] of the churches, a glory to Christ.
notes: Grk “If concerning Titus” (εἴτε ὑπὲρ Τίτου, eite huper Titou); the Greek sentence opens with an ellipsis which must be supplied: If [there is any question] about Titus.”
Grk “apostles.”

verses.zh: 所以，你们务要在众教会面前显明你们爱心的凭据，并我所夸奖你们的凭据。
verses.en: Therefore show[NOTE:1] them openly before the churches the proof of your love and of our pride in you.[NOTE:2]
notes: In the Greek text ἐνδεικνύμενοι (endeiknumenoi) is a present participle which is translated as an imperative verb (see BDF §468; ExSyn 650-52).tc The sense of this translation is attested by the fact that most of the later mss, along with several early and significant ones (א C D2 Ψ 0225 0243 1739 1881 M lat), have the imperative verb ἐνδείξασθε (endeixasthe) in place of the participle ἐνδεικνύμενοι (endeiknumenoi), which is found in B D* F G 33. Since an imperatival participle is more Hebraic in style, many scribes would not have understood the idiom as easily and would have been likely to change the participle to an imperative (so TCGNT 513-14). But there is no good reason why scribes would change the imperative into a participle. Thus, ἐνδεικνύμενοι is almost surely the wording of the original text.
Or “our boasting about you.”
